svg.title: Layered verification of LLM-agent-generated drug-discovery workflows
svg.desc: Four stages drawn left to right, each with its outcome below. 1, an LLM agent writes the code of an A2A receptor virtual screen; the decision under audit released 3 of 497 docked compounds. 2, ten executable contracts over nine gates, 94 checks, tested on 128 seeded faults: 124 detected under the benchmark's harness contract, 101 as deployed, and a simple snapshot comparison 128. 3, the contracts are challenged with blind-authored faults and metamorphic relations: 1 of 5 blind faults caught in a first round and 3 of 6 evaluable in a second, and rewriting molecules as equivalent SMILES changed all 25 docking scores. 4, the decision is reanalysed over the benchmark, eight descriptor spaces and the order of the rows: 72 of 5,000 compounds passed one filter in the released run, against a median of 1,004 over 200 reorderings. After one human-approved correction cycle, 3 of the 15 selected compounds persist under every analytic choice tested; persistence is not a prediction of activity. Contract coverage, decision stability and biomedical validation are reported separately.

After one human-approved correction cycle, a focus-library re-analysis selected 15 compounds
persistence: how many of the 15 are still selected under every analytic choice tested
